kinds.a: shentoi · shentai · Chinese home altar cabinet
kinds.d: Home altar cabinet holding deity images and ancestral tablets, with daily offerings of joss sticks and tea.
Placard marking the seat of an ancestor or deity, from a sheet of red paper to a carved wooden shrine.

x.d: Tablet kept in a cabinet or on an altar; ancestral tablets are regarded as holding the ancestor's soul.
x.dt: red paper written vertically · or wood

kinds.d: Paper talisman of Taoist script written or painted by a priest, hung above a door to ward off evil.

kinds.a: ghost money · spirit money · hell bank notes
kinds.d: Paper burnt as offering to gods and the dead: gold, silver and cash paper, hell bank notes and paper goods.

x.d: Modern joss paper in afterlife currency in denominations from ten thousand to five million; common among Cantonese populations.
x.dt: large denominations · Jade Emperor or Yanluo Wang portrait

kinds.a: kau chim · fortune sticks · chien tung
kinds.d: Cylinder of numbered bamboo fortune sticks shaken until one falls, to be read against a temple text.
Pair of crescent-shaped wooden blocks thrown to get a yes or no from a deity.
Ritual sword used to purify an altar and drive out evil; peach wood is held to protect against evil spirits.

x.d: Steel sword with the 28 Lunar Mansions and the Northern Dipper inlaid, used for exorcism and altar purification; probably never sharpened.

kinds.d: Octagonal or round mirror ringed with bagua trigrams, hung over a door to deflect harmful energy.

notes: Peach-wood sword: retrieved pages attest peach wood as protective and the steel Qing ritual sword, not a peach-wood sword itself. Household altar term shentoi/shentai appears only in a search snippet, so the kind rests on the Spirit tablet page.
